easy.question: Which coloured bin is meant for wet waste like fruit peels and leftover food?
easy.explanation: Wet waste such as fruit peels, vegetable scraps, and leftover food goes into the green bin. Dry waste like paper and plastic goes into the blue bin.

easy.question: Wet waste like vegetable scraps can be turned into ______, which is a natural fertiliser for plants.
easy.explanation: When wet waste is collected in a compost pit, microbes break it down over weeks into compost -- a rich, dark material that helps plants grow beautifully.

easy.question: Which of the following belongs in the blue (dry waste) bin?
easy.explanation: Dry waste includes paper, plastic bottles, wrappers, and cardboard. Banana peels, vegetable scraps, and leftover rice are wet waste.

easy.question: What does the Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya programme focus on?
options: Clean toilets, safe water, waste management, and hygiene in schools
easy.answer: Clean toilets, safe water, waste management, and hygiene in schools
easy.explanation: The Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya (Clean India Clean Schools) programme works to ensure every school has clean toilets, safe drinking water, proper waste management, and good hygiene practices.

easy.question: The village of ______ in Meghalaya is celebrated as Asia's Cleanest Village.
easy.explanation: Mawlynnong in Meghalaya earned the title of Asia's Cleanest Village because every person there, from children to elders, keeps the village spotlessly clean.

medium.question: What is a green school? Name four things a green school focuses on.
medium.answer: A green school is one where students, teachers, and staff work together to take care of the environment. The four main things it focuses on are: (1) handling waste responsibly by separating and composting, (2) conserving water, (3) using electricity wisely, and (4) making the campus greener by planting trees and nurturing gardens.
medium.explanation: A green school goes beyond just studying -- it creates an environment where everyone actively participates in keeping the school clean, safe, and sustainable.

medium.question: Why should we appreciate the work of sanitation workers and recyclers (kabadiwalas)?
medium.answer: Sanitation workers and recyclers play a vital role in keeping our surroundings clean and healthy. Sanitation workers collect and handle our waste every day. Recyclers (kabadiwalas) collect materials like paper, plastic, glass, and metal and send them to processing units where they are turned into new products, reducing the amount of waste that ends up in landfills. Without their hard work, our schools, streets, and neighbourhoods would be overwhelmed with garbage.
medium.explanation: These workers perform essential services that benefit the entire community. Their work deserves respect and gratitude from all of us.

hard.question: Your class decides to form three teams to improve the school environment. Name each team, explain what they would check, and suggest one action each team could take.
hard.answer: Three teams and their actions: (1) Water Watchers -- they would check for dripping taps, water wastage, and whether water tanks are clean and covered. They could start a rainwater collection system by directing rooftop rainwater to the school garden. (2) Waste Warriors -- they would check if students are using the correct bins, whether there is litter on the ground, and if waste is being separated properly. They could set up a compost pit for wet waste from the school canteen. (3) Green Guardians -- they would check the health of trees and plants on campus and look for birds and butterflies. They could organise a tree-planting drive and create a butterfly garden with flowering plants.
hard.explanation: Student teams empower children to take direct responsibility for their school environment. Each team focuses on a specific area and can make real, visible improvements.

topics.topic: Saving Water, Energy, and Staying Safe

easy.question: Which colour roof helps keep a building cooler in summer?
easy.explanation: White or light-coloured roofs reflect sunlight instead of absorbing it, helping keep buildings cooler. Dark-coloured surfaces absorb heat.

easy.question: During a fire at school, what is the first thing you should do?
options: Run back to collect your bag
Walk briskly toward the nearest exit without panicking
easy.answer: Walk briskly toward the nearest exit without panicking
easy.explanation: During a fire, stay calm and walk briskly to the nearest exit. Never hide, run back for belongings, or try to use the phone. Get out safely first.

easy.question: Earthen clay pots called ______ cool water naturally without using any electricity.
easy.explanation: Matkas cool water through evaporation -- water seeps through the tiny pores in the clay and evaporates on the outside, pulling heat away and chilling the water inside.

easy.question: Before crossing the road near school, what must you always do?
options: Look left, right, and left again
Close your eyes and hope for the best
Wait for someone else to go first
easy.answer: Look left, right, and left again
easy.explanation: Always look left, then right, then left again before crossing the road, and use the zebra crossing or pedestrian crossing whenever available.

medium.question: List three practical ways to save water at school.
medium.answer: Three ways to save water at school: (1) Report dripping or broken taps to the maintenance staff immediately so they can be fixed. (2) Always turn taps off completely after use and make sure they are not left half-open. (3) Set up rainwater collection from the school rooftop and use the collected water for the school garden.
medium.explanation: Small water-saving actions seem minor on their own, but when practised daily by hundreds of students, they save thousands of litres over a year.

medium.question: Why are trees valuable on a school campus? Give three reasons.
medium.answer: Trees are valuable on a school campus for many reasons: (1) They clean the air by absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing fresh oxygen for us to breathe. (2) They provide cool shade on hot days, making the campus more comfortable. (3) They attract birds, butterflies, and squirrels, making the campus lively and connecting students with nature.
medium.explanation: Trees improve air quality, lower temperatures, and support biodiversity. A school with many trees is healthier, cooler, and more pleasant for everyone.

medium.question: What are 'ice stupas' in Ladakh used for?
options: Providing water for gardens when ice melts in summer
medium.answer: Providing water for gardens when ice melts in summer
medium.explanation: Ice stupas are tall towers of ice built during winter in Ladakh. They slowly melt during summer, releasing water that is used to irrigate school gardens and farmland during dry months.

hard.question: A truly happy school is not just about clean buildings. What else is needed? Explain with examples of kind behaviour that make a school a better place.
hard.answer: A truly happy school also needs kindness, respect, and care in how people treat each other. Examples include: (1) Waiting patiently in line instead of pushing and shoving. (2) Using polite and encouraging words with classmates, teachers, and support staff. (3) Welcoming a new student who might be feeling lonely -- inviting them to sit with your group at lunch. (4) Never teasing or bullying anyone, because words can hurt deeply. (5) Keeping shared spaces like classrooms, playgrounds, and washrooms clean for everyone. (6) Showing respect to every person in the school, regardless of their role. When everyone practises kindness, the whole school becomes a place where students feel safe, included, and excited to learn.
hard.explanation: Physical cleanliness matters, but a school's happiness truly depends on how people treat each other. Kindness and respect create an environment where everyone can thrive.

hard.question: Describe the correct steps to follow during a fire emergency at school. Why should you never go back inside a building that is on fire?
hard.answer: Fire safety steps: (1) Stay calm and walk briskly toward the nearest exit -- do not run or push. (2) If there is smoke, crouch low or crawl because cleaner air is near the floor, and cover your nose and mouth with a cloth. (3) Never hide in cupboards, under desks, or in bathrooms -- rescuers cannot find you there. (4) Help younger or scared children by holding their hand and guiding them calmly. (5) Once outside, go to the assembly area and stay with your class group. (6) Tell a teacher immediately if anyone is missing or injured. You should never go back inside a burning building because fire spreads very rapidly and smoke makes it impossible to see or breathe properly. Going back puts your life in serious danger.
hard.explanation: Practising fire drills regularly helps everyone remember these steps so they can act quickly and calmly during a real emergency. The priority is always getting everyone out safely.
